verdict.line: You lose if you let Darius stack Hemorrhage to five before level 6; you win if you survive to Cannibalism and outscale off Enrage kills.

brief.thesis: Darius's Passive (Hemorrhage) turns every extended trade into a race to five stacks, and his Enrage bonus at max stacks is what gives him the 42.9% head-to-head edge over 163 games despite Sion sitting at 49.6% in the role overall. Sion has no way to interrupt that stack-up directly, so the matchup is decided by whether you can keep trades short with Q (Cryptic Gaze) and E (Enrage) rather than letting Darius get free autos in.

tell.watch: Darius's Hemorrhage stack count on you

theirWindow.what: Disengage immediately — a fifth stack triggers his Enrage attack damage spike, and he will chain Q (Decimate) and W (Crippling Strike) to finish the trade and heal off your minions.

yourWindow.what: Walk up and force a trade using Q (Cryptic Gaze) to stun him for free damage, since without the pull he has no way to punish you for engaging from range.

powerCurve.note: Hemorrhage stacks punish any early auto exchange
E (Apprehend) pull threatens every cannon wave
Your R (Cannibalism) sustain offsets his R threat
Core items online, Enrage health-to-damage scales up
Sunfire/Thornmail tank checks his all-in damage

start.why: The passive block and regen directly counter the chip damage from his autos and Q (Decimate) handle hits while Hemorrhage ticks, letting you hold cannon waves.

boots.why: Reduces the physical damage from his auto-attack-heavy trade pattern, which matters most since nearly all his damage before level 6 comes from basic attacks and Decimate.

core.why: Builds health and armor while adding a damage aura, which punishes him for standing in melee range to stack Hemorrhage.
The omnivamp and tenacity-style resolve kit sustains you through extended trades where he's trying to force max Hemorrhage stacks.
Directly answers his attack-speed reliant Enrage state by punishing every auto he lands on you once stacks are up.

situational.when: he is rushing lethality or crit items to burst through your health pool
you are ahead on kills off Enrage health stacking and want to push the wave advantage
the game is going long and you need a scaling health stat-check item

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp heals and grows your max health on proc, which stacks with your E (Enrage) health-to-damage conversion to make every short trade net you more sustain than Darius's Hemorrhage ticks take away.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 84.8% of games at this matchup's win rate because Teleport lets you reset after losing early trades to his Hemorrhage stacking without forfeiting the wave, which matters since you're behind on solo-kill potential.

playing.title: Count stacks before trading
playing.detail: Never commit to a second auto exchange once you're at 3+ Hemorrhage stacks — disengage and let them decay rather than risking his Enrage-boosted finisher.

playing.title: Stun on cooldown, not on cooldown reset
playing.detail: Use Q (Cryptic Gaze) the moment it's up (8-12s depending on rank) to interrupt his Decimate wind-up or punish an overextension, since it's your only hard engage tool.

playing.title: Track his E (Apprehend) before wave contests
playing.detail: Don't stand in his 535-range pull window near cannon waves; its 16-26.5s cooldown means there are long stretches where he can't threaten you at all.

playing.title: Enrage only in winning trades
playing.detail: Turn on E (Enrage) when you're ahead in a trade to convert health into AD, but toggle it off if the fight turns since it accelerates your own health loss.

playing.title: Save R for all-in windows
playing.detail: Cannibalism's 90s cooldown and attack-speed buff mean it's best saved for when you're forcing a kill, not a defensive panic button.

playing.title: Respect his R near 500 HP
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage scaled by your Hemorrhage stacks — if you're under five stacks it's far less threatening, so track stacks, not just his ultimate cooldown.

playing.title: Play for scaling, not lane dominance
playing.detail: You're not expected to win early trades at 42.9% head-to-head; prioritize surviving to your level 9-13 item spike where Sunfire and Thornmail swing fights your way.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being pulled by (E). Be careful of (P) when fighting him. Try to contest lane whenever your skills come off cooldown.
